title: Gaussian comparison for normalized Boolean sums
statement: There exists a constant $K>0$ such that for every positive integer $n$, every $c\geq0$, and every $c$-Lipschitz function $\psi\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, the uniform average of $\psi(n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\sigma(x_i))$ over Boolean vectors $x\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}^n$ differs from its integral under the standard Gaussian probability measure $\gamma$ by at most $Kc(1/n)^{1/4}$.
hypotheses_covered: The Boolean vector is averaged with the uniform product probability measure
The comparison measure is the standard Gaussian probability measure
replaced: There is a universal $K>0$ such that, for $n>0$, independent uniform signs $\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_n$, a standard Gaussian $Z$, and any $c$-Lipschitz $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ with $c\ge0$, $|\mathbb E\psi(n^{-1/2}\sum_i\epsilon_i)-\mathbb E\psi(Z)|\le Kc\,n^{-1/4}$.
